title: UK must not be beholden to foreign AI, says head of Alan Turing Institute
key_facts: George Williamson, head of the Alan Turing Institute (the UK's leading AI research body), says the UK must not depend on foreign AI systems that can be switched off at short notice.
He wants the UK to develop its own versions of the technology; 'national resilience' is the institute's key focus.

The Guardian notes that in June Washington temporarily blocked the release outside the US of Anthropic's latest models, and has reportedly asked leading AI labs to withhold models from the UK's AI Security Institute until its US counterpart has examined them.
The institute probably cannot match the financial resources of the major AI labs but could produce 'nationally owned IP' or smaller models for startups.
He doubted percentage estimates of AI-triggered extinction, saying nobody has shown convincing evidence for how they are reached.
The institute is under new leadership after the government, its main funder, demanded a strategic shift; Williamson is the former head of the Government Communications Centre.
ECB president Christine Lagarde and European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen have recently urged Europe to be more self-sufficient in AI.
quote_evidence: “As AI becomes more embedded in critical services, in domains like defence, national security, critical infrastructure and healthcare we shouldn’t depend solely on systems we can’t inspect or control, or that could be restricted or even switched off,” said Williamson.

In June Washington temporarily blocked the release outside the US of Anthropic’s latest models, and has reportedly asked leading AI labs to withhold their models from being tested by the UK’s AI Security Institute until they have been examined by AISI’s US counterpart.
“We can be ambitious here without trying to copy what frontier labs are doing,” he said.
why_it_matters_hint: A UK science leader argues for home-grown AI as protection against supply cut-offs.
